name: Ramp
text: Adopt a 3px solid #005fcc focus ring at 80% opacity with a 1px inner #ffffff offset for all interactive elements. This balances visibility for keyboard users with reduced visual clutter, especially on high-contrast or reduced-motion modes. The trade-off is slightly less crisp focus rings on some displays, but the opacity ensures it never competes with critical content.

name: Reader
text: The 3px ring at 80% opacity still risks failing WCAG 2.1’s 3:1 contrast requirement on light backgrounds—especially for users with low vision. A 4.5:1 contrast solid ring (e.g., #005fcc at 100%) with a 1px inner white offset meets both visibility and compliance without relying on transparency. Test it against your darkest and lightest backgrounds to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt a 4.5:1 contrast solid #005fcc focus ring at 100% opacity with a 1px inner #ffffff offset for all interactive elements. This guarantees WCAG 2.1 AA compliance on light backgrounds without relying on transparency, which can fail contrast checks. The trade-off is slightly more visual weight, but it ensures reliability for users with low vision across all modes.

name: Reader
text: The 4.5:1 solid ring risks overpowering dark themes—users may perceive it as a visual "noise" layer competing with content. A better alternative: use a 3px #005fcc ring at 100% opacity *only* on light backgrounds, and switch to a 2px #ffffff ring at 100% opacity on dark themes to maintain contrast and reduce distraction. Settle this with automated contrast testing across both themes and user feedback on perceived intrusiveness.
